name: Lake Tisza Anglers: Shore Site Ranking
description:
Faithful replication of Benkhard et al. (2025), "Recreational and Landscape Preferences of Anglers in the Case of Lake Tisza", Land 14:600. The template follows the paper's 19-question survey (Appendix C). Participants are shown eight pictures of typical Lake Tisza shore sites (different angling-spot size, vegetation, water-surface width and opposite-shore vegetation; Figure 4 / Appendix A) and rank three of them for angling, for a longer stay of several days and for a shorter stay, each time explaining why in their own words. The survey also asks where and how often they angle, their purposes at the lake, ten site-selection factors (1 = not at all, 5 = completely), the most beautiful seasons, other landscapes they travel to and for what purpose, and residence, age, gender, education, income and money management. Analysis as in the paper: dichotomise each ranking (selected / not selected), report the share choosing each picture and ranking it first, code the open answers into categories (shade, natural vegetation, beauty, angling, camping, open water, peace and quiet, infrastructure), and describe the Likert items. In the original study (224 anglers interviewed in spring 2024), picture 2 was chosen most often for angling (62%) and longer stays (57%), picture 8 was ranked first most often, and picture 4 was chosen most often for short stays.

Pictures: the paper's Figure 4 (photographs of Lake Tisza shore sites; article CC BY 4.0), each about 360 × 280 pixels, used with credit; the template is removed if the authors object.

Differences from the original study: (1) the original was an in-person interview with a printed picture montage; here it is a self-completed online page, and pictures are chosen by tapping instead of writing their numbers; (2) the eight pictures are cut from the paper's Figure 4 without the colour key, so they are small; (3) "Other" answers to questions 2 and 17 go into a separate text field; question 12's table is shown as one row of purpose checkboxes per landscape; (4) the shorter-stay ranking and all "why" questions can be skipped, matching the high share of missing answers reported for short stays; (5) an online consent checkbox was added; the wording is the English version printed in the paper's Appendix C.
author: Benkhard et al.
